questions.question: Which mountain range crosses Switzerland, Austria and Italy?
questions.explanation: The Alps are about 1,200 kilometres long. Many people go skiing there in winter and walking in summer.

questions.question: Which country is shaped like a boot?
questions.explanation: Italy sticks out into the Mediterranean Sea like a long boot. It even looks as if the boot is kicking the island of Sicily.

questions.question: Which sea has Spain, France, Italy and Greece on its coast?
questions.explanation: The name means "middle of the land". The sea lies between Europe, Africa and Asia.

questions.question: Which island country in the North Atlantic has volcanoes and geysers?
questions.explanation: Iceland sits on a crack between two huge plates of the Earth's crust. That is why it has so many hot springs and volcanoes.

questions.question: Which country is known for its long, deep fjords?
questions.explanation: Fjords are narrow sea inlets with steep sides. Ice carved them thousands of years ago.

questions.question: Which country is famous for its windmills and tulips?
questions.explanation: The Dutch used windmills to pump water off low land. Every spring, the tulip fields turn into bright stripes of colour.

questions.question: Which tiny country lies inside the city of Rome?
questions.explanation: Vatican City is the smallest country in the world. It is less than one square kilometre in size.

questions.question: Which two seas touch the coasts of Denmark?
questions.correct: The North Sea and the Baltic Sea
wrong: The Black Sea and the Baltic Sea
The North Sea and the Red Sea
The Baltic Sea and the Adriatic Sea
questions.explanation: Denmark is made up of a peninsula and hundreds of islands. No place in Denmark is far from the sea.

questions.question: Which large island lies just west of Great Britain?
questions.explanation: Ireland has a mild, wet climate, so its fields stay green all year.

questions.question: Which stretch of sea separates England from France?
questions.explanation: At its narrowest point, the Channel is only about 33 kilometres wide. Since 1994, trains have gone through a tunnel under it.

questions.question: Which Alpine country is known for cheese, chocolate and watches?
questions.explanation: Switzerland has no coast, but it has many mountains and lakes. It has four national languages.

questions.question: The Øresund Bridge links Copenhagen with which Swedish city?
questions.explanation: The bridge is almost eight kilometres long. It meets a tunnel on a man-made island called Peberholm.

questions.question: What do we call Norway, Sweden, Denmark, Finland and Iceland together?
questions.explanation: The word Nordic means "northern". The Faroe Islands, Greenland and Åland are part of the Nordic family too.

questions.question: Copenhagen lies mostly on which Danish island?
questions.explanation: Zealand is the biggest Danish island, if you do not count Greenland. Funen lies to the west of it.

questions.question: Which sea lies east of Sweden and north of Poland?
questions.explanation: The Baltic Sea is not very salty, because many rivers flow into it and little water flows in from the ocean.

questions.question: The Netherlands is low and flat. What do the Dutch build to keep the sea out?
questions.explanation: A dike is a high wall of earth along the coast or a river. Pumps then take the water away from the land behind it.

questions.question: Which country in the United Kingdom is known for its Highlands and lochs?
questions.explanation: A loch is the Scottish word for a lake. Many of them lie between high hills.

questions.question: Which small island country lies south of Sicily?
questions.explanation: Malta is made up of a few small islands. People there speak Maltese and English.

questions.question: Which country is sometimes called "the Hexagon" because of its six-sided shape?
questions.explanation: A hexagon has six sides. France has sea or mountains on most of its sides.

questions.question: Which country in south-east Europe has more than a thousand islands, such as Crete and Rhodes?
questions.explanation: Most of the islands are very small, and nobody lives on them. Many people visit the bigger ones on holiday.

questions.question: Odense, where H.C. Andersen was born, lies on which Danish island?
questions.explanation: Funen lies between Zealand and Jutland. It is sometimes called the garden of Denmark.

questions.question: Which region in the far north of Sweden, Finland and Norway is known for reindeer?
questions.explanation: The Sami people have kept reindeer in Lapland for hundreds of years. In winter you can see the northern lights there.

questions.question: The island of Mallorca is a holiday island in the Mediterranean. Which country does it belong to?
questions.explanation: Mallorca is the biggest of the Balearic Islands. Its neighbours are Menorca and Ibiza.

questions.question: Which country lies directly west of England on the island of Great Britain?
questions.explanation: Wales has its own language, Welsh. Its mountains include Snowdon.

questions.question: Which of these islands belongs to Denmark?
questions.explanation: Bornholm lies far out in the Baltic Sea, closer to Sweden than to the rest of Denmark.

questions.question: Which ocean lies to the west of Portugal and Ireland?
questions.explanation: The Atlantic stretches all the way from Europe and Africa to the Americas.

questions.question: Which country next to the Netherlands is famous for waffles and chocolate?
questions.explanation: Belgium also has a short coast on the North Sea. People there speak Dutch, French and German.

questions.question: Which of these countries has no coast on any sea?
questions.explanation: Austria lies in the middle of Europe and is mostly mountains. A country with no coast is called landlocked.

questions.question: Greenland and the Faroe Islands are part of the kingdom of which European country?
questions.explanation: Greenland is the biggest island in the world. It lies far away, off North America.

questions.question: Which large country in south-west Europe has the cities of Barcelona, Valencia and Seville?
questions.explanation: Spain covers most of the Iberian Peninsula. It also has islands in the Mediterranean and the Atlantic.

questions.question: Which three countries are usually called Scandinavia?
questions.explanation: Danish, Norwegian and Swedish are so close that people from the three countries can often understand each other.

questions.question: Which country lies between Germany and Ukraine and has a coast on the Baltic Sea?
questions.explanation: Poland has flat land in the north, and the Tatra Mountains on its southern border.

questions.question: The town of Billund has the first Legoland park. In which country is it?
questions.explanation: Billund lies in the middle of Jutland. The Lego company started in this small Danish town.

questions.question: Which big Swedish port city lies on the west coast, facing Denmark?
questions.explanation: Gothenburg lies on the Kattegat. Ferries sail from there to Denmark and Germany.

questions.question: Which part of Europe has hot, dry summers and many olive trees?
questions.correct: The coasts of the Mediterranean Sea
questions.explanation: Olive trees like long, hot, dry summers and mild winters. This climate is found in Spain, Italy and Greece.

questions.question: Which country lies directly north of England, on the island of Great Britain?
questions.explanation: Scotland and England share a land border. Wales lies to the west of England.

questions.question: Which large country lies directly east of the Netherlands?
questions.explanation: The Netherlands has Belgium to the south and Germany to the east. The North Sea is to the north and west.

questions.question: Which very large country covers the east of Europe and the north of Asia?
questions.explanation: Most Russians live in the European part, west of the Ural Mountains. Much of the land east of the Urals is called Siberia.

questions.question: In midsummer the sun does not set in northern Norway. What is this called?
questions.explanation: North of the Arctic Circle the sun stays up all night in midsummer. In winter it is the other way round, with weeks of darkness.

questions.question: Which is the highest mountain in the Alps?
questions.explanation: Mont Blanc is about 4,800 metres high. It stands on the border between France and Italy.

questions.question: Which large city lies on both sides of the Bosporus, in Europe and in Asia?
questions.explanation: A narrow strait splits Istanbul in two. Bridges and ferries join the European side to the Asian side.

questions.question: Which peninsula in south-eastern Europe includes Greece, Bulgaria and Albania?
questions.explanation: The Balkans take their name from a mountain range in Bulgaria. Many peoples and languages meet there.

questions.question: Which three countries make up Benelux?
questions.explanation: The name is made from the start of each country's name. The three agreed in 1944 to trade freely with each other.

questions.question: Which tiny country lies between Switzerland and Austria?
questions.explanation: Liechtenstein is only about 25 kilometres long. It lies in the Alps, next to the River Rhine.

questions.question: Which tiny country lies high in the Pyrenees between France and Spain?
questions.explanation: Andorra is a small mountain country. People go there to ski and to shop.

questions.question: Which tiny country sits on the Mediterranean coast, with France on all its land sides?
questions.explanation: Monaco covers only about two square kilometres. It is one of the most crowded countries on Earth.

questions.question: Which Danish island is known for its tall white chalk cliffs above the Baltic Sea?
questions.explanation: The cliffs, called Møns Klint, rise more than 100 metres above the sea. The chalk formed from tiny shells on an old sea floor.

questions.question: Which Dutch city has a huge port near the mouths of the Rhine and the Maas?
questions.explanation: Goods from all over the world arrive in Rotterdam. Then ships, trains and lorries take them on across Europe.

questions.question: Which city in Tuscany is known as the birthplace of the Renaissance?
questions.explanation: Florence is in central Italy. Great artists such as Leonardo da Vinci and Michelangelo worked there.

questions.question: Which Russian city did Peter the Great build on the coast of the Baltic Sea?
questions.explanation: He founded the city in 1703 on marshy land by the sea. It was the Russian capital for about 200 years.

questions.question: Which Norwegian city lies north of the Arctic Circle and is known for the northern lights?
questions.explanation: In the middle of winter the sun does not rise in Tromsø for weeks. In summer it does not set.

questions.question: Which mountains are usually seen as the border between Europe and Asia in Russia?
questions.explanation: The Urals run from north to south for about 2,500 kilometres. They are old, rounded mountains.

questions.question: Which sea lies between Italy and Croatia?
questions.explanation: Venice lies at the top of the Adriatic. The sea is named after the old Italian town of Adria.

questions.question: Which three countries are called the Baltic states?
questions.explanation: The three countries lie on the eastern shore of the Baltic Sea. Each has its own language.

questions.question: Which Alpine country has the cities of Innsbruck and Salzburg?
questions.explanation: Both cities are close to the mountains. Salzburg is the birthplace of the composer Mozart.

questions.question: About how much of the Netherlands lies below sea level?
questions.explanation: Dikes, dunes and pumps keep the water out. Part of the land used to be seabed.

questions.question: Which mountain range runs along the border between Norway and Sweden?
questions.explanation: The range is about 1,700 kilometres long. It is also called the Scandes.

questions.question: The Wadden Sea has mudflats along the coasts of Denmark, Germany and which other country?
questions.explanation: At low tide you can walk on the sea floor. Millions of birds stop there to eat.

questions.question: Which small Alpine country is known for Lake Bled and its island church?
questions.explanation: Slovenia has Alps, a short coast on the Adriatic and many caves.

questions.question: Which country has the Dalmatian coast, with many islands in the Adriatic Sea?
questions.explanation: The cities of Split and Dubrovnik lie on this coast. The Dalmatian dog gets its name from the region of Dalmatia.

questions.question: Which German state has the cities of Munich and Nuremberg?
questions.explanation: Bavaria is in the south of Germany. It is the biggest German state by area.

questions.question: Which French region is famous for its fields of lavender?
questions.explanation: Provence is in the south of France. In summer, its fields turn purple and smell sweet.

questions.question: Which sea lies between Great Britain and Ireland?
questions.explanation: Ferries sail across the Irish Sea between cities such as Liverpool and Dublin.

questions.question: Which small country borders Belgium, France and Germany?
questions.explanation: Luxembourg is about 80 kilometres long. It is one of the smallest countries in Europe.

questions.question: Which large German city lies on the Rhine, between Bonn and Düsseldorf?
questions.explanation: Cologne is known for its huge Gothic cathedral, which took over 600 years to finish.

questions.question: Transylvania, a region of forests and castles, lies in which country?
questions.explanation: Transylvania is inside the curve of the Carpathian Mountains. It means "the land beyond the forest".

questions.question: Bohemia, with its old towns and forests, is a region of which country?
questions.explanation: Bohemia is the western and biggest part of Czechia. Prague lies in the middle of it.

questions.question: Spain's Canary Islands lie in the Atlantic Ocean, off the coast of which continent?
questions.explanation: The islands belong to Spain but lie about 100 kilometres from the African coast. Spain's highest mountain, Teide, is a volcano on Tenerife.

questions.question: The Channel Islands, such as Jersey and Guernsey, lie close to the coast of which country?
questions.explanation: The islands are not part of the United Kingdom, but the UK looks after their defence.

questions.question: Barcelona is the main city of which region of Spain?
questions.explanation: Catalonia lies in the north-east of Spain. Its people speak Catalan as well as Spanish.

questions.question: Which large French port city lies on the Mediterranean coast?
questions.explanation: Marseille was founded by Greek sailors about 2,600 years ago. It is one of the oldest cities in France.

questions.question: The Great Belt Bridge links Zealand with which Danish island?
questions.explanation: The bridge and a rail tunnel cross the Great Belt strait. Before they opened, people had to take a ferry.

questions.question: Which Norwegian city on the west coast is known as the gateway to the fjords?
questions.explanation: Bergen lies between seven mountains and is known for its rain. Boats and trains take visitors from here to the big fjords.

questions.question: Which French region has Mont-Saint-Michel and the D-Day beaches?
questions.explanation: Normandy lies on the Channel coast in the north-west of France. Mont-Saint-Michel is a rocky island with an abbey on top.

questions.question: In which country is Flanders, where people speak Dutch and the cities include Ghent and Bruges?
questions.explanation: The north of Belgium is Flanders. The south is Wallonia, where people mostly speak French.

questions.question: Which Italian region has the city of Milan and Lake Como?
questions.explanation: Lombardy is in northern Italy, below the Alps. It is a busy region for business and fashion.

questions.question: The Mont Blanc Tunnel runs under the Alps and links France with which country?
questions.explanation: Cars and lorries drive through the tunnel instead of over the high mountain passes.

questions.question: Which region of southern Spain has the cities of Seville, Córdoba and Granada?
questions.explanation: Andalusia is hot and dry in summer. It is known for flamenco and for buildings from the Moorish time.

questions.question: Which Swiss city lies on the Rhine, right where Switzerland, France and Germany meet?
questions.explanation: The borders of the three countries meet in the Rhine at Basel. The city's airport lies in France and is run by France and Switzerland together.

questions.question: Which river flows from Czechia through Dresden to the North Sea?
questions.explanation: The Elbe starts in the Giant Mountains. It meets the North Sea near Cuxhaven in Germany.

questions.question: Which river forms much of the border between Germany and Poland?
questions.explanation: The rest of the border follows the Neisse, a river that flows into the Oder. The Oder then flows north to the Baltic Sea.

questions.question: Which strait between Denmark and Norway leads from the North Sea towards the Baltic Sea?
questions.explanation: The Skagerrak lies north of Jutland. Further south, the Kattegat leads on towards the Baltic Sea.

questions.question: Which German state lies directly south of Denmark?
questions.explanation: Until 1864, the Danish king ruled Schleswig and Holstein. A Danish minority lives in the north of the state.

questions.question: The puszta in Hungary is a large area of what?
questions.explanation: On the puszta, herders once looked after cattle and horses on the open plain.

questions.question: The Camargue, with wild white horses and pink flamingos, is a wetland in the delta of which river?
questions.explanation: The Camargue lies in southern France, where the Rhône meets the Mediterranean.

questions.question: Lake Ohrid, one of the oldest lakes in Europe, lies on the border of Albania and which country?
questions.explanation: The lake is very deep and clear. Many animals there live nowhere else.

questions.question: Which region forms the "heel" of Italy's boot?
questions.explanation: Puglia, also called Apulia in English, is known for olive trees and white towns. Calabria is the "toe" of the boot.

questions.question: At which German city do the Rhine and the Moselle meet?
questions.explanation: The place where they meet is called the Deutsches Eck, the "German Corner".

questions.question: On which river does the German city of Frankfurt lie?
questions.explanation: The full name of the city is Frankfurt am Main, which means "Frankfurt on the Main".

questions.question: Which sea lies between southern Italy and western Greece?
questions.explanation: The Ionian Sea is part of the Mediterranean. Its islands include Corfu and Kefalonia.

questions.question: Which two countries are completely surrounded by Italy?
questions.explanation: San Marino sits on a mountain called Monte Titano. It is one of the oldest republics in the world.

questions.question: Which river flows through the middle of Berlin?
questions.explanation: The Spree starts in the hills near the Czech border. In Berlin it passes the Museum Island.

questions.question: The Jura mountains lie along the border between France and which country?
questions.explanation: The Jura gave its name to the Jurassic period, because rocks there are from that age.

questions.question: Which country lies directly south of Estonia?
questions.explanation: The border runs through a twin town: Valga is in Estonia and Valka is in Latvia.

questions.question: Lake Peipus lies on the border between Estonia and which country?
questions.explanation: Lake Peipus is large but shallow. It is one of the biggest lakes in Europe that crosses a border.

questions.question: Which river forms most of the border between Romania and Bulgaria?
questions.explanation: The Friendship Bridge between Ruse in Bulgaria and Giurgiu in Romania opened in 1954.

questions.question: Which gulf of the Baltic Sea lies between Helsinki and Tallinn?
questions.explanation: Helsinki and Tallinn are only about 80 kilometres apart across the water.

questions.question: Which Belgian port city lies on the River Scheldt?
questions.explanation: Antwerp is a huge port, even though it lies about 80 kilometres from the open sea.

questions.question: What is the large mountain area in the middle of southern France called?
questions.explanation: It has many old volcanoes, such as those of the Auvergne.

questions.question: What is the large high plateau in the middle of Spain called?
questions.explanation: The Meseta covers a large part of inland Spain. Madrid stands on it.

questions.question: Which Dutch province is made almost entirely of land reclaimed from the sea?
questions.explanation: Most of it was pumped dry in the 1950s and 1960s, and it became a province in 1986.

questions.question: Which river flows through the Scottish city of Glasgow?
questions.explanation: Great ships such as the Queen Elizabeth 2 were built on the Clyde.

questions.question: Which river flows through the German city of Munich?
questions.explanation: The Isar starts in the Alps and joins the Danube. Munich's people like to relax on its banks in summer.

questions.question: Which river flows through Seville in southern Spain?
questions.explanation: The name comes from Arabic and means "the great river". In the 1500s, ships from the Americas sailed up it to Seville.

questions.question: In which Italian region is the city of Venice?
questions.explanation: Veneto lies in the north-east of Italy. Its other well-known cities include Verona and Padua.

questions.question: Which Portuguese city lies at the mouth of the River Douro?
questions.explanation: The country's name comes from this city. Its old name was Portus Cale.

questions.question: Which Danish fjord runs right across northern Jutland, from the North Sea to the Kattegat?
questions.explanation: Because of it, the land to the north, Vendsyssel-Thy, is really an island. The biggest island in the fjord is Mors.

questions.question: Which river flows through Turin and across northern Italy to the Adriatic Sea?
questions.explanation: The Po is the longest river in Italy. Its valley is the country's biggest plain.

questions.question: Santiago de Compostela, an old pilgrim city, is in which region of Spain?
questions.explanation: Galicia lies in the north-west corner of Spain. Many pilgrims walk the Camino de Santiago to the city.

questions.question: At which French city do the Rhône and the Saône meet?
questions.explanation: Lyon is built on the two rivers. It was an important Roman city.

questions.question: Which Polish port on the Baltic Sea was once known by its German name, Danzig?
questions.explanation: Gdańsk was a rich trading town of the Hanseatic League. It stands near the mouth of the Vistula.

questions.question: Llívia is a small Spanish town surrounded by France. In which mountains does it lie?
questions.explanation: Llívia is an enclave: a piece of Spain inside France. A treaty in 1659 gave France villages, but Llívia was a town and stayed Spanish.

questions.question: Büsingen is a German village completely surrounded by which country?
questions.explanation: Büsingen am Hochrhein is a German enclave on the north bank of the Rhine, next to the Swiss town of Schaffhausen.

questions.question: Which cold, strong wind blows down the Rhône valley in southern France?
questions.explanation: The mistral can last for days. It brings clear skies, and in Provence it bends the trees.

questions.question: Silesia is a region with coal, old towns and the city of Wrocław. In which country does most of it lie?
questions.explanation: Silesia also reaches into Czechia and Germany. The River Oder flows through it.

questions.question: Strasbourg lies on the Rhine, by the German border. In which historic French region is it?
questions.explanation: Alsace has a mix of French and German styles. Many half-timbered houses look more German than French.

questions.question: In which Swiss region do most people speak Italian?
questions.explanation: Ticino lies south of the Alps, with palm trees and warm lakes. Lugano and Locarno are its main towns.

questions.question: Which country lies between Romania and Ukraine?
questions.explanation: Moldova has no coast. The Prut River runs along its border with Romania.
